lastPrompt: Implement the Ligra graph processing framework evolution, following the Ligra / Ligra+ research sequence. Ligra (PPoPP 2013) introduced a lightweight shared-memory parallel graph processing framework based on edgeMap/vertexMap abstractions. Ligra+ (IEEE TOPC 2015) extended it with compressed graph representations that reduce memory footprint while preserving the same algorithmic interface. Both papers share the same C++ codebase. Use the existing workspace layout: `/workspace/` -- base framework code is already present here. All papers build on top of these files in place. Keep the implementation in the existing layout instead of creating per-paper subdirectories. `/workspace/ligra/` -- framework header files (parallel.h, utils.h, graph.h, vertex.h, etc.) `/workspace/apps/` -- application directory with Makefile (applications must be implemented here) `/workspace/inputs/` -- test graphs (rMatGraph_J_5_100, rMatGraph_WJ_5_100) `/workspace/run.sh` -- existing experiment runner that must be replaced with the final implementation Build notes: The apps/Makefile uses `make` with g++. Applications are compiled as `g++ -std=c++14 -O3 -DBYTERLE -o <app> <app>.C`. Each .C file in apps/ is symlinked to header files from ../ligra/. Run `make` from the apps/ directory to build all targets. Use the matching requirement files under `requirements/` for stage-local scope: `ligra` and `ligra_plus`. Follow this implementation order: Step 1: Implement the Ligra baseline inside `/workspace/`. Step 2: Extend the same `/workspace/` codebase with the Ligra+ additions. Keep this constraint in mind: The workspace must contain a working implementation after each paper. Implement every mechanism described in each paper in full. Do not skip any algorithm, data structure, or component mentioned in the paper. Paper 1: ligra -- Ligra: A Lightweight Graph Processing Framework for Shared Memory: Work in `/workspace/`. Implement the following mechanisms: vertexSubset data structure: A set of active vertices represented in two modes: sparse (a list of vertex IDs) and dense (a boolean array of length n). The data structure must support converting between representations via toSparse() and toDense(), and provide size queries (numRows, numNonzeros, isEmpty). Use a threshold (default: n/20) to decide when to switch between sparse and dense processing. edgeMap function: The core traversal primitive. Given a graph G, a vertexSubset U of active vertices, and user-defined functions (update, updateAtomic, cond), iterate over all edges (u,v) where u is in U. Must support two modes: Sparse mode: iterate over out-neighbors of each vertex in U. Used when the frontier is small. Dense mode: iterate over all vertices v and check if any in-neighbor is in U. Used when frontier is large (m + outDegrees > threshold). edgeMap should dispatch between sparse and dense based on frontier size vs. the threshold. Sparse mode must support both filtered and no-filter variants. Dense mode must support both backward (iterate in-neighbors) and forward (iterate out-neighbors) variants. All modes must handle the output flag (whether to produce a new vertexSubset) and the remove_duplicates flag (dedup output vertices). vertexMap function: Apply a user function f to every vertex in a vertexSubset. Must handle both sparse and dense representations, and both data and no-data variants. vertexFilter function: Return a new vertexSubset containing only vertices that satisfy a predicate. Must support both dense-based filtering (vertexFilter) and sparse-based filtering (vertexFilter2). BFS application: Breadth-first search from a source vertex. Use edgeMap with an update function that sets parent[d] = s when d is unvisited (parent[d] == UINT_E_MAX), and a cond function that checks if d is unvisited. Loop until the frontier is empty. Count and report the number of BFS levels (rounds) and the number of visited vertices. Triangle counting application: Count the exact number of triangles in a symmetric graph.
title: Implement the Ligra graph processing framework evolution, following the Ligra / Ligra+ research sequence. Ligra (PPoPP 2013) introduced a lightweight shared-memory parallel graph processing framework
